subject: On-demand fallback & latency agreement — post-call notes and next steps
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alya Thomas <alya@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 19 Jul 2026 16:12:00 -0700
Subject: Post-call: on-demand fallback & latency targets (recap + proposal)

Hi Alya / Ravi — thanks again for taking the time today. Quick recap from our discovery call and a compact proposal so we have alignment before the POC: 

1) Core SLO targets you asked us to validate (proposal):
- Interactive requests (single-turn, short outputs): p95 generation latency <= 250ms, p99 <= 600ms
- Streaming / chat first-token latency: median <= 120ms, p95 <= 300ms
- Sustained token throughput: 150k tokens/min per model shard during peak windows
- Concurrency: baseline 800 concurrent active sessions, burst to 3,200 with fallback queueing

2) Autoscaling / burst behavior (proposal):
- Warm pool: maintain 150 prewarmed instances (fractional split across regions) for <100ms cold start coverage for most short requests
- On-demand scale-up: cold scale path from zero to full capacity in ~60-90s depending on model size; fast-path (warm pool hit) in <150ms
- Queueing policy: Token-cost-aware queue with capped wait-time SLO of 8s before transparent fallback (reduced-quality model or degraded stream mode)

3) Observability & gating for SLO acceptance:
- We’ll instrument p50/p95/p99, first-byte streaming metrics, queue wait distributions, and per-route token accounting for a 2-week POC window.
- Run two traffic profiles: normal-day (75th pct load) and stress-window (95th-99th pct) to validate autoscale ramp and fallback behavior.

Attachments: I attached an initial SLO spreadsheet (slo-draft.xlsx) with proposed thresholds and a quick warm-pool sizing sketch.

Next steps I recommend:
- You confirm the proposed SLO numbers or mark ones to relax/tighten by EOD Wed
- We schedule a 60-min POC kickoff (suggest Wed 21 Jul or Thu 22 Jul) to lock in traffic profiles and test plan
- Redwood will provide a short mutual action plan and a one-week test harness with synthetic load for the initial validation

If you want, I can also put together a brief note on the fallback degraded-mode UX so your product folks can evaluate impact.

Thanks —
Ben

From: Alya Thomas <alya@fastpay.com>

Subject: Re: Post-call: on-demand fallback & latency targets (recap + proposal)

Ben — thanks for the clear recap. A few clarifying Qs from our side before we lock dates: 

- Warm pool sizing: how did you arrive at 150 prewarmed instances? Can you give an example calculation (concurrency per instance, expected token rates)?
- Scale-up time: our compliance folks insist any on-demand path must not take >2m for full capacity. You wrote 60-90s; is that the 95th percentile or an average?
- Fallback behavior: if the queue exceeds 8s, what does the degraded UX look like? Will tokens be truncated or will we switch to a smaller model with the same prompt?

Also, we need a basic commercial note for FastPay procurement on how burst charges will be accounted during the POC. Can Marissa or someone on your team send an outline?

If possible, let's aim for the kickoff Thu 22 Jul in the morning ET.

—Alya
Alya Thomas
Head of Platform Engineering, FastPay
alya@fastpay.com
From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Alya Thomas <alya@fastpay.com>, Ravi Shah <ravi.shah@fastpay.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Jul 2026 12:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Post-call: on-demand fallback & latency targets (recap + proposal)

Alya — thanks, good questions. Answers inline and a short plan: 

- Warm pool calculation (brief): 150 prewarmed instances = (target baseline concurrency 800 / avg concurrency-per-instance 6) * safety factor 1.9.
  - Example: one prewarmed instance handles ~6 active short sessions (typical short request pattern). At 150 instances that gets us ~900 active sessions on warm-path. We split 60/40 across primary region and DR region. Details in warm-pool-plan.pdf.

- Scale-up time clarification: the 60-90s estimate is a 75th-90th percentile for our cold-start scale path for medium-sized models (7–13B). Larger model families may observe ~120–180s at p95. We will include percentile targets in the POC. The 2-minute procurement constraint is reasonable; we’ll design the POC to validate p95 < 2m.

- Fallback degraded UX options (we recommend two modes):
  1) Graceful downgrade: transparently route to a smaller, quantized model variant with maintained prompt context (slightly lower quality). User sees slightly shorter output but no hard failure.
  2) Streaming degraded mode: begin streaming first-byte quickly with a note that higher-fidelity completion will follow off-band (useful for time-sensitive UX).
  - We can exercise both modes during the stress window and measure user-visible latency and quality deltas.

Commercial stub: Marissa — can you draft a short POC commercial note that covers baseline credits, burst charges, and an interim billing cap for FastPay? Alya — I’ll send a simple breakdown (expected token units for the two-week POC) once Marissa gives the baseline.

Proposed kickoff: Thu 22 Jul 2026 09:30–10:30 ET — is that workable?

I attached the warm-pool-plan.pdf with the sizing math and a short note on split-region behavior. Also attaching fastpay-mvp-specs.docx you mentioned.

Ben

Attachments: warm-pool-plan.pdf, fastpay-mvp-specs.docx

Alya — looping in the commercial/eng handoff. Thanks for the thoughtful questions.

Immediate commercial notes (POC):
- Redwood will provide a two-week POC: baseline credits to cover normal-day traffic plus a capped burst allowance. We’ll propose a one-time POC fee that covers tooling and ops support; any overage beyond the capped burst will require approval.
- Deliverables before kickoff: mutual action plan doc, test harness instructions, HubSpot record with test accounts (HS-4982).

Operational ask for the kickoff:
- FastPay to provide two representative routes with sample prompts/output size estimates and a single synthetic traffic profile (we’ll provide the script).
- Redwood will provision warm pool per the attached plan and run the normal/stress windows. We’ll share per-minute metrics and a short daily readout.

Ben — please prepare the mutual action plan and the token estimate by EOD Wed (21 Jul). Alya — once you confirm the kickoff time we’ll lock calendar and send the docusign POC agreement.
